newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 27.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* The market is likely to drift upwards as the bottom may have been reached, said Dharmala Securities Philippines analyst Manuel Goseco. Clients are recommended to enter into a cautious accumulation phase with an eye on blue chips.
* Turnover will still be light ahead of the release of first quarter GNP figures and as heavy rains on Monday may keep local investors at bay, analysts said.

* The Philippine stock market was closed on Monday minutes after it opened due to bad weather. The stock market's composite index was at 2,601.86 points, up 3.66 when trading was stopped. PSE Governor Harry Liu said trades on Monday would be credited to Tuesday's session.
* On Friday, the main index rose 11.51 points to 2,598.20.
* The U.S. financial and equity markets were closed on Monday for the Memorial Day holiday. On Friday, the Dow Jones rose 87.78 points to 7,345.91. PLDT's ADR rose $01/8 closing $55 1/4.
* The Philippine peso closed untraded at 26.375 to the dollar on Monday
* Money market trading was also suspended due to the inclement weather. The Philippine interbank call loan average on Friday was at 18.03125 percent.
* At least 29 people died as torrential rains battered the Philippines on Monday, flooding thousands of homes and bringing the capital to a standstill.

* The National Coalition of Coconut Farmers' Organisation said it is opposing a deal recently entered into by Philippine food firm San Miguel Corp and Coca-Cola Amatil over its local Coca-Cola operations.
* Philippine Central Bank govrenor Gabriel Singson said the Monetary Board was studying the possibility of imposing a stricter rule on banks' foreign exchange assets to make them liquid.

* The Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) said it sees 1997 coconut production at 2.6 million tonnes compared with 2.4 million tonnes in 1996. Exports will reach $900 million with $867 million in 1996 while export volume is seen at about 1.6 million to 1.8 million tonnes against 1.5 million tonnes in 1996.
* Philippine sugar millers, pinched by an influx of cheap imports, have pleaded for government protection to enable the industry to compete with other sugar-producing countries.
* Newspapers Inquirer and the Business Daily reported that the Lippo Group of Indonesia is finalising negotiations on the purchase of Prime Savings Bank, a local thrift bank.
* BusinessWorld said the National Power Corp lowered industrial power rates by 0.48 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) on Monday after the approval by the Energy Regulatory Board last February.

* The Manila Bulletin reported tht the Department of Transportation and Communications wants the National Telecommunications Commission to study the possible application of price caps in the setting of access charges among telephone carriers finalising interconnection agreements.
* The Chronicle said the Bankers Association of the Philippines has urged the Central Bank not to impose caps on banks' exposure to foreign currency deposit units (FCDUs).
